summary: Priority-band saturation from orchestrator heartbeats causing intermittent 429s for interactive requests
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sudden spikes of 429 responses for low-latency interactive requests starting 2026-03-01 ~09:30 UTC. Impact: user-facing timeouts and degraded chat UX for a subset of their users on a dedicated pool. Initial observation shows large volume of short POST /v1/heartbeat calls originating from their orchestrator service that appear to be consuming credits in the interactive priority lane rather than a background/bulk lane. This looks like quota exhaustion at the tenant/prioritized-lane level, not model-side failures.

Impact: ~15% of interactive requests are rejected during bursts, retries cause increased latency and customer-visible errors.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-vestigo-eu-w1), production, us-west edge path. Customer has a mixed workload: orchestrator control-plane (heartbeats, health checks, small metadata updates) + interactive chat sessions.

Requested outcome: clarify why heartbeats count against the interactive quota, provide immediate mitigation steps and a fix plan to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs orchestrator which issues 1-2s interval POST /v1/heartbeat requests from 50 workers (simulating prod).
2) Simultaneously issue interactive chat requests (streaming) from same tenant API key across 20 sessions.
3) Observe occasional 429 responses for chat sessions with headers indicating priority-lane exhaustion and Retry-After small values.
4) Reproduce more consistently by increasing heartbeat fanout to 200 short requests/second from orchestrator and observe 429 propagation to interactive lanes.
observed_logs: 2026-03-01T09:32:14.256Z edge-gw [trace=tr-9a1c] POST /v1/chat/stream 429 t=1ms tenant=vestigo route=interactive-priority X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 Retry-After=6
2026-03-01T09:33:01.001Z quota-svc [trace=quota-554] Tenant=vestigo priority_band=interactive refill_window=60s available=0 consumed=12000
Sample trace-id: tr-9a1c (edge-gw) -> quota-554 (rate-limiter) -> scheduler-02 (ingress rewrite)
comments: 2026-03-01 10:05 - Maya Patel: Customer reports spike started after they enabled more aggressive orchestrator probes during a canary rollout. They see 429s for chat users intermittently; provided telemetry and API key.

2026-03-01 10:22 - SRE (Anika Shah): Added preliminary rate-limiter traces and requested packet captures from customer. Hypothesis: short-lived heartbeats are being classified as interactive due to an ingress path rewrite rule used by their proxy.

2026-03-01 12:01 - Customer (Alex Chen, Vestigo): Confirmed they recently changed the orchestrator to reuse the same route path /v1/heartbeat with interactive routing header for consistency. Will test switching to background path if supported.
2026-03-02 09:18 - Liam Oconnor (Support): Applied temporary console override to treat /v1/heartbeat from vestigo's API key as background for edge-us-west. Monitoring for reduction in 429s.
2026-03-02 11:43 - Vestigo: After override, chat 429s dropped to <1% during same heartbeat load. Reporting improved UX.
investigation_notes: Telemetry shows a sustained 8-10k/s short-request rate from the customer's orchestrator during peak that was hitting the interactive priority_band token window and driving refill to depletion.

Ingress gateway route inspection: request path /v1/heartbeat matched an ingress rule that carries interactive route metadata header (x-rw-route=interactive). The customer's proxy explicitly sets that header for uniform observability.

Quota accounting: rate-limiter attributes are computed from (tenant, priority_band, route) where route metadata trumped intent. Heartbeats therefore consumed interactive pool credits instead of background pool.

Root cause: configuration mismatch + ingress header semantics change in customer's orchestrator. Edge gateway respected header and placed requests into interactive lane. No bug in refill algorithm, but lack of route isolation allowed control-plane telemetry to compete with user traffic.
Related signal: small Retry-After values seen, but backoff amplification from orchestrator's dense polling pattern amplified impact on interactive requests.
temporary_workaround: 1) Support applied console route override to remap path /v1/heartbeat for tenant vestigo to background-priority lane on prod-us-west. This reduced interactive 429s immediately.
2) Recommended the customer lower heartbeat frequency from 1s -> 10s for orchestrator control-plane until permanent fix is rolled out.
3) Advised customer to stop sending the interactive routing header from the orchestrator when the intent is a control-plane/background workload.
4) Customer can also enable per-route burst isolation ('isolate_burst_pool') for the heartbeat path if they want permanent isolation on their side.
resolution: 2026-03-03: Engineering fix merged to edge-gateway that prioritizes explicit console route mappings over ingress-provided route headers for customers on Dedicated pools where route isolation is configured (PR https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4532).
Support verified in prod-us-west for Vestigo: interactive 429s dropped from ~15% to <0.5% under same orchestrator load after the console mapping and edge-gateway change.

Follow-ups: update runbook to include guidance for dedicated customers about control-plane vs interactive route classification, add console UI toggle for 'treat-ingress-headers-as-trustworthy' per-tenant, and a telemetry alert when short-request ratio > 20% of interactive pool consumption.
next_steps: 1) Close monitoring window for 72 hours; if no regression, move to Resolved and perform post-incident review.
2) Product to expose per-tenant setting for ingress-header trust and per-route burst isolation by 2026-04-15.
3) Customer to revert orchestrator header change and adopt background path or reduce heartbeat frequency.
4) Runbook and support KB update to include this pattern and recommended configs for Hybrid workloads on Dedicated pools.
